function: Joint downlink channel estimation from limited pilots (RIS-CENet at the UE) and quantized CSI compression and feedback (RIS-CFNet) in an RIS-aided FDD system (p. 1, p. 3).
system: RIS-aided multi-user FDD downlink: BS with 16-antenna ULA, reflecting RIS with 64 units (planar array), 6 single-antenna users; frequency band not stated (p. 2, p. 4).
method: CNN with dual-channel attention (RIS-CENet) plus Transformer encoder-decoder (RIS-CFNet) with 2-bit quantizer; supervised MSE; distributed training, UE encoder and BS decoder exchange gradients (p. 2, p. 3, p. 4).
data_channel: Own simulated Rician channels, BS-RIS, RIS-user, BS-user links (Rician factors 10, 0, 0; path-loss exponents 2.3, 2, 3.6); dataset size not stated (p. 2, p. 4).
test_conditions: Same simulated setup for training and testing; test sweeps over SNR -15 to 15 dB, compression ratio 2-8 and 2-6 users; no unseen scenario (p. 4, p. 5).
baselines: Estimation: LS, MMSE (non-learned); CDRN [5], EDSR [7] (learned). Feedback: CsiNet, CLNet, CRNet (learned); centralized-training versions of the proposed schemes (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR, compression ratio and number of UEs; model size, FLOPs, parameters and inference time (p. 4, p. 5).
complexity: Table II: UE and BS model size, FLOPs, parameters and inference time on an RTX 4090; scheme II UE 0.016 GFLOPs, 6.702 M parameters, 0.780 s (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "All channels adopt the Rician fading model"; Table I (p. 4) gives Rician factors and path-loss exponents of a custom simulator, and no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 4: "different SNR and CR, as well as the NMSE comparison"; p. 5: "illustrates that as the number of UEs increases, the NMSE"; only SNR, compression-ratio and UE-count sweeps on one simulated setup, with no unseen scenario, band or fine-tuning, and no model trained at one K and tested at another.
q3_support: p. 4: "Fig. 4 illustrates the NMSE performance of different channel estimation methods"; p. 4: "compared to other deep learning schemes"; Fig. 4 (p. 4) plots LS and MMSE with learned CDRN [5] and EDSR [7], and Fig. 5 plots CsiNet [8], CLNet [19] and CRNet [20], all on NMSE.
q4_support: p. 5: "Table II compares the storage space and computational"; Table II (p. 5) lists model size, FLOPs, parameters and inference time for the UE and the BS, e.g. scheme II UE 0.016 GFLOPs, 6.702 M parameters, 0.780 s.
q5_support: p. 4: "The simulation experiment utilizes MATLAB as the communication link simulation platform"; the channels are the authors' own simulation (Table I), the dataset size is not given, and no code or data link, DOI or release statement appears in the paper.
notes: PDF checked: title and DOI 10.1109/LWC.2024.3509612 on p. 1 match. Area 2: the learned networks do joint channel estimation and feedback; the 'distributed learning' is UE-encoder and BS-decoder training with gradient exchange, not over-the-air aggregation, so not area 7. Tables I and II and the figure legends were read from the images of pp. 4-5, because they are missing from the extracted text; the Fig. 4 legend reads EDSR [7]. q3: the estimation network is compared with LS and MMSE and with CDRN and EDSR (Fig. 4); the feedback network is compared only with learned CsiNet, CLNet and CRNet (Fig. 5). q2: p. 1 claims better adaptation to changing environments, but no experiment tests unseen conditions, and Fig. 8 does not say a model trained at one K was tested at another.
